clue.text: Evil spirit in island area exorcised by us

indicators.note: exorcised means driven out, so the letter for area is expelled from the island's name

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A demon on an island is driven from the district by us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exorcised' suits the evil spirit in the surface, but here it only drives one letter out of the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a male demon of folklore said to visit sleepers, a kind of malign spirit.

clue.text: I proceed to nab a villain

indicators.note: to nab is to seize or catch, so the words I and proceed together grab hold of the letter a

parts.note: to proceed is to go

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to arrest a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nab' puts A inside I + GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The schemer of Shakespeare's Othello is literature's archetypal villain.

clue.text: Things people wear, such as belt or sock

definitions.meaning: British slang for clothes or gear
both mean hit hard, as in a verb for beating someone

explanation.surface: A list of clothing items, belts and socks among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' and 'sock' look like garments continuing the list, but they are verbs meaning to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word both for one's clothes and gear and, as a verb, for striking someone heavily.

clue.text: Sound of colonel's truck

indicators.note: sound of tells us the word to write is one that is pronounced like the colonel's name

parts.note: Colonel Bogey is the imaginary golfer of a famous British march tune

explanation.surface: The noise made by an army officer's lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colonel Bogey March is a well-known British military tune; the wheeled undercarriage of a railway vehicle is spelt differently but pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In railway terms the word names a wheeled undercarriage, a small truck on which a carriage pivots.

clue.text: Aircraft in winter has to miss out part of route

parts.note: to miss out a step is to skip it
a lane is a division of a road or route

explanation.surface: A winter flight must skip a stretch of its usual path.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light plane fitted with skis instead of wheels so it can land on snow, hence a winter aircraft.

clue.text: Finally he commits crime and he gets away

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the two words he and commits

parts.note: a caper is a criminal escapade or heist

explanation.surface: A man commits a crime and flees at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' applies to both 'he' and 'commits', giving E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who escapes, a fugitive, is a man who gets away.

clue.text: Weak, lacking energy in the end: catching cold the result?

indicators.note: catching means taking in, so the cold letter is captured inside the shortened word
lacking means going without, so the energy letter is dropped from the word for weak
in the end says the letter dropped is the final one of the word for weak

parts.note: effete means feeble or weak
E is the physics symbol for energy
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A feeble, drained person catches a chill, and that is the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking energy in the end' drops the last E of EFFETE to leave EFFET; 'catching' puts C inside it before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: An effect is an outcome or consequence of a cause.

clue.text: Cut both cereal and dessert, then fast — being this?

definitions.text: Cut both cereal and dessert, then fast — being this?

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, and both says the trimming applies to each of the two foods named

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop
pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Advice to give up cereal and pudding and fast, as if you were overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut both' docks the last letter of CORN and of PUD, giving COR and PU; the whole clue suggests why someone might diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very fat, overweight, is why someone would cut out cereal and pudding and then fast.

clue.text: Arrive, though match cancelled in such circumstances?

definitions.meaning: to turn up somewhere, often unexpectedly
a game is called off when the playing field is torn up or unplayable

explanation.surface: Someone turns up only to find the game has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a sports ground that is dug up means no match.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to arrive or turn up, and read literally describes a playing field that has been torn up.

clue.text: Dealt with customers in bank in diffident way

indicators.note: in places the shop-counter phrase inside the word meaning depend on

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a shop assistant who dealt with customers served them

explanation.surface: A shy bank clerk attended to customers timidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun for the place, but it is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with reserve means behaving in a restrained, shy manner.

clue.text: My turn to fix old fridge that's on the blink

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

indicators.note: on the blink means malfunctioning, so the letters of fridge come out in a broken order

explanation.surface: Someone takes their turn at repairing an ancient, faulty fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation of surprise; FRIDGE rearranged gives DGRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or dismay, interchangeable interjections.

clue.text: Charges for lectures

definitions.meaning: fees or prices set per unit
as a verb, scolds or tells off severely

explanation.surface: The fees someone pays to attend talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lectures' looks like a noun for talks, but it is a verb meaning scolds, an old sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means fees or tariffs; as a verb, to berate someone angrily.

clue.text: Given the boot, worker — beginning to think about career — has look round

parts.note: a worker bee

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word think
round means surrounding, so the word for look goes around the other two pieces

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly
C, short for circa, means about
to career is to rush headlong

explanation.surface: A sacked worker, starting to consider a new career, looks around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given the boot' reads as sacked, but 'the boot' is the definition; 'career' is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: This is humorous British slang for a large heavy shoe, especially a big boot.

clue.text: Deck with lots of people

parts.note: a pack of cards used to tell people their lots, that is their fates or fortunes, not a crowded ship's deck

explanation.definitionFit: A fortune teller's pack is used to read the fate, or lot, of the people consulting it.

clue.text: Plant, one stunted in a polluted environment

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened word goes inside the other pieces
environment means surroundings, so the a and the polluted word surround the stunted piece

parts.note: grimy means dirty or polluted

indicators.note: stunted means cut short, so the last letter of one is lost

explanation.surface: A plant grows only a little in a dirty, smoggy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a verb, but it is the noun; 'in' and 'environment' together frame the container, and 'stunted' trims the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a yellow-flowered herb of the rose family, a wild plant.

clue.text: College production of endgame enthrals nearly everyone

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so the rearranged letters hold the shortened word
a production makes something new out of materials, so the letters of endgame are reworked
nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A college stages a chess endgame that captivates almost the whole audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College' is the definition, not a hint at a university setting; 'production of' signals the rearrangement and 'enthrals' the insertion. Magdalene is a Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalene is one of the colleges of Cambridge University, and Oxford has a similarly named one.

clue.text: Little bird's sob story

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: A small bird tells a sad tale.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE for magpie is a crossword staple, as in the name magpie itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearjerker, a sentimental film or book meant to make you cry, is a sob story.

clue.text: Troubled person receives expression of sympathy

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the word for person contains the sympathetic word

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person
there, there is said to comfort someone

explanation.surface: A worried man is comforted by kind words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worried or upset is being troubled.

clue.text: Popgun going off in dispute

indicators.note: going off as a gun firing, or as food spoiling, signals the letters of popgun are scrambled

explanation.surface: A toy gun fires in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' reads as a gun firing; it is the signal to rearrange POPGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare verb means to call into question or argue against, so to contest or challenge.

clue.text: Guide dog

definitions.meaning: something that indicates direction, such as a hint or an indicator needle
a gun dog breed that stands rigid to indicate game

explanation.surface: A dog trained to lead the blind.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, a guide dog, but each is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a hint or indicator, and also a breed of hunting dog that indicates game.

clue.text: Measure liberal and labour backed is a controversial issue

parts.note: a foot is a unit of measure

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the liberal letter and the labour word are read backwards

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the British Labour Party

explanation.surface: A political measure backed by both Liberals and Labour stirs up controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like support, but it turns L + LAB round to give BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A political football is an issue kicked around between parties for advantage.

clue.text: Us inhabitant aboard steamer in Delaware

indicators.note: aboard means carried within, so the answer sits inside the words steamer in Delaware

explanation.surface: An American passenger is on a ship in an eastern US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is written to look like the pronoun, but read it as US, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old term for a Native American, an original inhabitant of the Americas.

clue.text: From attack, allowed to run away

parts.note: let means allowed
to fly is to flee or run away

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to escape an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a verbal or physical assault, to lash out, is to attack.

clue.text: Chemical agent affected global warming

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters of chemical agent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemical substance has had an impact on the warming planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The rise in the Earth's temperature from greenhouse gases is the main shift in the planet's weather patterns.

clue.text: Was he a poet? Write wrong answer first, then correct one

parts.note: no as a negative reply that is wrong
yes as the right reply

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a poet, answered wrongly then rightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes wrote the ballad The Highwayman; the definition is a question because the answer is his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman.

clue.text: Staff sergeant expecting meal heads over here

definitions.text: Staff sergeant expecting meal heads over here

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the run of first letters is read backwards
heads points to the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A staff sergeant awaiting dinner goes to the place where soldiers eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes S, S, E, M; 'over' reverses them to make the answer, the place the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A military dining hall where service personnel eat together is where a hungry sergeant would go.

clue.text: Mostly fairly prompt, in former times

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: rather means fairly or somewhat

explanation.surface: A remark that someone was largely on time in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word meant early or quick, so prompt in old usage.

clue.text: Number in favour of northern banker seizing home

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the river's name holds the word for home

parts.note: a river has banks, and the Tyne is a river in northern England
in means at home

explanation.surface: A count is in favour of a northern banker who takes over a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' means a river, something with banks; the Tyne flows through Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure seven times seven is a number.

clue.text: Well at first, later ropy, with heart failing — this may be needed

definitions.text: Well at first, later ropy, with heart failing — this may be needed

parts.note: to well up is to surge

indicators.note: the heart of the word ropy, its middle, fails and drops out, leaving first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone well at first, then poorly with a weak heart, may need an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropy' is British slang for unwell; losing its middle letters leaves RY.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation by a doctor is what may be needed when someone's heart is failing.

clue.text: Party drinks going over sofa

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: going over means flipping round, so the word for drinks is read backwards

parts.note: sodas are fizzy drinks

explanation.surface: Partygoers spill their drinks over the couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sofa' is the definition, not the thing the drinks are spilt on; 'going over' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a seat or sofa built so that two people sit back to back.
